legacy.interpretation: All 41 catalogue phases were decoded and inspected: reveal/highlight of a fixed building, not recovered mechanical operation or camera rotation. All actual profile catalogue roles map to AC03.VID. Two surface descriptors are shadow/body. Shared ACS2 construction is an existing separate contract; no AC-named _MA family is present.

concept_attempts.feedback: Retains the bell housing and flared base, copper bulb, asymmetric brass facing, grille/status lens and two external pipes feeding blue-gray aggregates. Accepted as an interpreted detailing guide; the upper bulb/finial were kept modest in the model to favour the actual legacy proportions. Seams, clamps and hidden intake depth are authored interpretations.

glb_feedback.observation: Actual native/import renders retained the main legacy massing and pipe equipment. The lower intake frame was partly buried in the flared base despite correct ray depths inside all 15 cells.
glb_feedback.action: Reduced the vertical extent of the flare and moved the intake slightly upward. Added actual casing-ray checks that each rim corner straddles the housing surface.

glb_feedback.observation: The corrected rim is visibly seated. The status lens was now too low relative to the shifted grille and the original raster.
glb_feedback.action: Moved the lens beside the upper part of the grille and verified the relative bounds on both saved native and independently imported GLB.

glb_feedback.observation: Final real front-quarter/front/rear views retain the copper/brass/blue-gray silhouette and restrained wear. The intake remains a real pocket with a rear well and 15 open ray paths, not an uncut wall with painted cells.
glb_feedback.action: Accept for integration review. Actual pixel parity verifies export representation, not an exact percentage of legacy fidelity. Hidden rear details and client state/scale remain explicitly unestablished.

review: Legacy-led static remaster, ready for client integration review. The camera is an approximate front-quarter interpretation, not a recovered original projection. No final user artistic acceptance, FPS guarantee or operational timing is claimed.
